{{Short description|American sociologist, statistician, and education researcher}}
{{Orphan|date=December 2024}}

'''George William Bohrnstedt''' (born September 28, 1938, Arcadia, WI) is an American sociologist, statistician, and education researcher.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |date=2021-12-15 |title=George Bohrnstedt |url=https://www.air.org/experts/person/george-bohrnstedt |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=American Institutes for Research |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Bohrnstedt received his PhD from [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] in 1966<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1571-284X |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> under the supervision of Edgar F. Borgatta.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Borgatta |first=Edgar F. |last2=Bohrnstedt |first2=George W. |date=1966 |title=Elementary Forms of the Quick Word Test |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00220973.1966.11010985 |journal=The Journal of Experimental Education |language=en |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=57–61 |doi=10.1080/00220973.1966.11010985 |issn=0022-0973|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He spent most of his 20-year academic career at the [[University of Minnesota|University of Minnesota-Twin Cities]] and [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University-Bloomington]] and was chair of the Department of Sociology at both universities.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |date=2024-12-12 |title=Bohrnstedt, George W. |url=https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/author/george-w-bohrnstedt?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=SAGE Publications Inc |language=en}}</ref><ref name="auto"/> In 1988 he moved to the [[American Institutes for Research]] where he was active as Senior Vice-president and Institute Fellow until his retirement in March of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-15 |title=George Bohrnstedt |url=https://www.air.org/experts/person/george-bohrnstedt |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=American Institutes for Research |language=en}}</ref>

One of his statistics articles  "On the exact covariance of products of random variables" (with Arthur S. Goldberger)<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bohrnstedt |first1=George W. |last2=Goldberger |first2=Arthur S. |date=December 1969 |title=On the Exact Covariance of Products of Random Variables |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01621459.1969.10501069 |journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association |language=en |volume=64 |issue=328 |pages=1439–1442 |doi=10.1080/01621459.1969.10501069 |issn=0162-1459|url-access=subscription }}</ref> which appeared in the ''Journal of the American Statistical Association''  has been cited in research articles in areas as diverse as psychology, chemistry, electrical engineering, forestry, operations research, and genetics.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |title=George Bohrnstedt |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=YMOoiAMAAAAJ&utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

His textbook ''Statistics for Social Data Analysis'' co-authored with David Knoke (and Alicia Potter Mee for the 4th edition) is widely cited and was used in the teaching of upper level first year graduate level statistics courses.<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=George W. Bohrnstedt {{!}} Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences |url=https://casbs.stanford.edu/people/george-w-bohrnstedt?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=casbs.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref>   He also co-edited ''Sociological Methodology: 1969'' with Edgar F. Borgatta) and the two of them were also the founding editors of ''Sociological Methods and Research''<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto2"/>''. '' He was also served the editor of ''Social Psychology Quarterly'' from 1979 to 1982.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto1"/>

Bohrnstedt was also the leader and clarinetist with the ''Riverboat Ramblers'',<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2Z4ME1v1VGw |title=Riverboat Ramblers 2008 - Track13 |date=2010-05-28 |last=jazzfesztivalhu |access-date=2024-12-17 |via=YouTube}}</ref> a popular traditional band that regularly played venues in the Madison, Milwaukee, and Lake Geneva areas of Wisconsin in the 1960s.<ref>{{Citation |title=The Riverboat Ramblers - Up The Creek With The Riverboat Ramblers |date=1968 |url=https://www.discogs.com/release/13811691-The-Riverboat-Ramblers-Up-The-Creek-With-The-Riverboat-Ramblers?srsltid=AfmBOoqUXokfqLJ-dlsI35FjoSxn01B2Y3Ow1-fTtfwp1WmXyAnooJ2_ |access-date=2024-12-17 |language=en}}</ref>
